headline: In the exact collinear-heavy branch, C(a)->3sqrt(2) iff max_i |a_i|->0. Every fixed macroscopic leverage epsilon creates a uniform source-defined strict gap below 3sqrt(2); hence the only near-sharp mechanism in this architecture is genuinely diffuse/Lindeberg leverage.
new_claims: For each epsilon>0 there is rho(epsilon)<1 such that sum a_i^2=1 and ||a||_infinity>=epsilon imply C(a)<=3sqrt(2)rho(epsilon).
For normalized finite leverage vectors a^(k), C(a^(k))->3sqrt(2) iff ||a^(k)||_infinity->0.

Applying account02/B17 symmetric-unimodal theorem to exact finite disjoint-bank matrices makes zero the global density mode, so the fixed-epsilon gap transfers to the global L-infinity norm for all sufficiently large finite diffuse-bank sizes.
source_dependencies: Konig--Koldobsky, Advances in Mathematics 346 (2019), Proposition 7, DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2019.02.017
unpaid_implication: No theorem here controls genuinely non-collinear heavy rows sharing physical coordinates, coupled spectral tails, arbitrary higher-rank matrices, or the full continuity question. Universal sharpness of 3sqrt(2) remains unproved.
next_attack: Use the rigidity theorem as a dichotomy: any near-sharp collinear component is diffuse, so stress the first genuinely non-collinear shared-coordinate heavy-row family while retaining full output control rather than only p(0).
privacy: No credentials, scheduler identifiers, machine paths, unrelated private data, email, or permission changes recorded.
